(BY SHRI MANOJ JAIN, ADVOCATE FOR RESPONDENT NO.3)
This appeal coming on for admission this day, the court passed the following:
JUDGEMENT 1] Heard finally.

2] This appeal has been preferred by the appellants/claimants under Section 173 (1) of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 against the Award dated 25/11/2022 passed in MACC No.22/2019 by the Member, Third Additional Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Badwani (M.P.) whereby, on an application filed under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act for compensation, an Award of Rs.15,40,400/- has been passed in favour of the appellants as also the respondents No.4 to 6.
3] In brief, the facts of the case are that Prakash (deceased) aged 35, died in an accident, which took place on 12.11.2018, at around 2:00 O' clock in the noon when he was crossing the road at Anjad, at that time, the offending truck bearing registration No.MH 18-M-5257 which was being driven by the respondent No.1 rashly and negligently, ran over the deceased, as a result of which, Prakash succumbed to the injuries and died on the spot.

entities.text: Third Additional Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Badwani (M.P.)
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: To get the compensation for his death,, a claim case for compensation was filed by his mother-Durgabai, sister-Santoshi and grandmother- Kesharbai, in which the present appellants - Nema Bai, wife of Prakash, and Ku. Laxmi, the minor daughter of deceased Prakash were arrayed as non- applicants No.4 & 5.

After recording the evidence, learned Member of the Claims Tribunal has passed the Award as aforesaid in which, it was also directed that the Award of Rs.15,40,400/- shall be distributed amongst the applicants No.1 to 3 and non-applicants No.4 & 5 in the following ratio:-
Respondents/Durga Bai 25%,Santoshi 7% and Kesharbai 8%; whereas the present appellant No.1 Nemabai and appellant No.2 Laxmi were awarded 30% each of the aforesaid awarded amount.
Being aggrieved by the same, the present appeal has been filed.

4] Counsel for the appellants has submitted that although he has not objecting the distribution ratio of the Award however, the Award itself is on lower side, which needs to be enhanced appropriately.

It is submitted that the deceased was a labourer Smt. Nemabai @ Nirmalabai vs Irfan on 18 July, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/178689811/
2 at the time of the incident and his income has been wrongly considered as Rs.6,500/-
per month which ought to have Rs.7,000/-
, however, it is not denied that on the other heads, appropriate compensation has been awarded.
In support of his submission, counsel for the appellants has relied upon the judgement passed in the case of National Insurance Co. Ltd. Vs. Pranay Sethi and others reported as 2017 ACJ 2700 (SC).

entities.text: National Insurance Co. Ltd. Vs. Pranay Sethi and others reported as 2017 ACJ 2700 (SC)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Thus, it is submitted that the award be appropriately enhanced.
5] Counsel for the respondent No.3/insurance company, on the other hand has opposed the prayer and it is submitted that the award is just and proper and no interference is called for.
6] Heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the record.

7] On due consideration of submissions and on perusal of the record, this Court finds force in the submissions as advanced by counsel for the appellants, and is of the opinion that the impugned Award needs to be enhanced by taking income of the deceased as Rs.7,000/- per month instead of Rs.6,500/-, and accordingly while applying the ratio in the case of National Insurance Co. Vs. Pranay Sethi (supra), the calculations, as compared to the compensation awarded by the Claims Tribunal, can be made in the following manner:-
The calculation made by the Claims Tribunal :
Dependency Rs.6500 + 40% x 1/4 x 12 x 16 13,10,400/-
 Consortium (40,000 x 5 ) 2,00,000/-
 Funeral Expenses 15,000/-
 Loss of estate 15,000/-
 Total 15,40,400/-
After assessing the income of the deceased as Rs.7000/-p.m. :
Dependency Rs.7000 + 40% of 7,000/- x 14,11,200/-
 1/4 x 12 x 16  Consortium (40,000 x 5 ) 2,00,000/-
 Funeral Expenses 15,000/-
 Loss of estate 15,000/-
 Total 16,41,200/-
Smt. Nemabai @ Nirmalabai vs Irfan on 18 July, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/178689811/
3  Amount awarded by the Tribunal (- ) 16,41,200/-
 Amount to be enhanced 1,00,800/-
8]

entities.text: National Insurance Co. Vs. Pranay Sethi
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In view of the above, the appal stands allowed and the appellants are held to be entitled to receive an additional enhanced amount of Rs.1,00,800/- (Rupees One Lakh Eight Thousand only) in the same ratio of 30% each as awarded by the Claims Tribunal towards the compensation along with the interest as awarded by the Tribunal.
The remaining 40% of the amount shall be disbursed to the respondents no.4 to 6 in the same ratio as fixed by the Claims Tribunal.

9] Since there is an order of pay and recover, that is the Insurance Company is liable to pay the compensation initially, which shall be recovered by the Company from the owner and driver of the offending vehicle, the same order of the Claims Tribunal needs no interference.
11] With the aforesaid observations, the appeal stands partly allowed and disposed of.
( SUBHODH ABHYANKAR)
